images.text: With some trepidation, Ted and Ramona walked up to the door of the magnificent marble house. Ted thought that the vacation home would be a nice anniversary surprise for his wife. He knew that he really shouldn't have paid for such a luxurious rental, but he also realized that spontaneous romantic gestures were important in a relationship.

"What do we do to get in?" Ramona wondered out loud.
"I think we put our finger on this little scanner over here. It's supposed to read our fingerprints," Ted said.
“I should have known,” said Ramona. “This whole place is wired with cutting-edge technology.”
Ramona scanned her finger, and the door slid open. She gasped. She had never been in such a high-tech mansion in her life.
"How do you turn the lights on, Ted?" she asked, turning to her husband.
"Just ask the butler," Ted said with a grin.
"What?" Ramona giggled.
"Say, 'Butler, turn lights on!'" With that, all the lights in the house came on.

Suddenly, Ramona thought that she heard soft music playing. She couldn't believe it. It was their song! The one that had been playing on the radio when they'd first kissed!
"Oh, Ted," Ramona smiled, "you're such a sweetheart. How did you get it to do that?"
"Well," Ted replied sheepishly, "I asked them to sync all of our favorite songs before we came."
“That's so sweet,” Ramona said. “You should have programmed in our favorite drinks as well,” she added facetiously.
Ted understood that she was joking, but he just winked. “Try it, why don't you?” he said, grinning.
“Butler, bring us two vodka martinis,” Ramona requested.
Almost immediately, a robotic butler wheeled in from the kitchen, with their drinks on a silver platter.
"Here's to us," said Ted, grabbing a glass. "What do you think?”
“I'm considering moving in permanently," replied Ramona, smiling.
“I guess I should have told you,” said Ted. “We only have the rental for one evening.”
“In that case, we'd better get our money's worth,” replied Ramona. “Butler, bring me a shrimp cocktail and a tray of caviar!”

You can use perfect modals to talk about unfulfilled obligations or things that you regret doing or not doing.
You use the structure should have + past participle or shouldn't have + past participle to:

• talk about unfulfilled obligations in the past.

    For example:
    You should have returned the car on time. Now you have to pay an extra charge.

  • talk about regrets.

    For example:
    I should have tried harder at work. Now I have to look for another job. I shouldn't have said those things to my boss - he doesn't like me now!

You use some verbs that describe mental states with the Present Continuous to emphasize that you have recently started to think about something or that you are not sure about something.

Verbs that describe mental states are:
find
realize
regret
think
understand

Compare these two examples:
I regret that the company is to be folded. (I regret the decision and I'm sorry about it)
I'm regretting my decision to hire him. (I'm increasingly aware that this was the wrong decision)
You use the verb consider in the Present Continuous to mean think carefully about.

For example:
I'm considering taking a vacation at the end of the year.
